newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Nordic Telecom giants leap on merger rumours.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nordic Telecom giants leap on merger rumours.

text.p: Shares in Swedish telecommunications rivals LM Ericsson AB AB and Finnish rival Nokia Oy rose sharply on Wednesday on market rumours the two were planning a merger.
Both companies quickly denied the rumours and market players themselves said they doubted there was any basis to them.
Ericsson closed 9.5 crowns higher at 206 and in Helsinki Nokia closed 7.0 markka up at 255 markka.
"It merely seems like market players are trying to explain a sharp upturn by pointing to merger rumours," one broker said.
Another broker said: "Rumours are buzzing about Ericsson and Nokia merging, but I don't think anyone believes it."

Ericsson, Nokia and Motorola are the world's three largest mobile telephony companies. Market talk of mergers involving a grouping of two or more of the concerns have been consistently denied in the past.

Market analysts have never excluded the possiblity of a merger between one of Nokia, Ericsson and Motorola, but a link-up has more commonly been rumoured between the U.S. company and one of the European concerns to give a better geographical spread.
Ericsson spokesman Lars Stalberg told Reuters the Stockholm-based company never commented on such talk: "We never comment on rumours like this. If we have something to say, we will."
Privately, sources at Ericsson said there was little sign of the frenetic activity that would be connected to a merger that would create the world's largest mobile telephone company.
Nokia spokesman Seppo Harkonen echoed the Ericsson comments: "Company policy is not to comment on rumours in or from the market," he said.
The rumours began in mid-afternoon in Sweden at one of the quietest times of the year. "I suspect part of the market has been out at Christmas celebrations," one trader said.
Many brokers in Helsinki dismissed the rumours but said they had helped move Nokia stock.
The Ericsson surge contributed to massive turnover totalling 7.44 billion crowns on the Stockholm bourse, a record for the year.
The general index jumped 1.7 percent to 2297.50. In June, 1994, the all-time high of 10.5 billion was reached. -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
